You might be interested in Rand Paul's "Flat Tax" proposal.

Essentially it eliminates most deductions and credits, treats all income the same and taxes income over $50,000 at 14.5%. While it is not quite what you described or I would have proposed it is a huge step in the right direction. Unfortunately many people dismiss it since it is called a "flat tax". While the percentage is indeed flat, the exclusion of the first $50,000 in income makes it quite progressive -- that is income of $50,000 is taxed at 0%; $100,000 is taxed at 7.25%; $200,000 is taxed at 10.875%; $1,000,000 is taxed at 13.775%. The more one makes the closer to 14.5% your effective tax rate is.

FYI, the median US Family income in 2013 (the latest number I could find) was $52,250. This means the median US family would pay $362.25 in Federal Income Taxes and have an effective tax rate of 0.69%.

The simplification of the tax code combined with the equity of closing many loopholes that only benefit the wealthy makes this a huge step forward.
